messages:
Aisha: Quick question  if latency steering would pick us-west but account policy says EU-only, which wins?

Tom: Policy wins. We should never violate explicit residency.

Lena: Agree. But there are many customers who want 'prefer EU' not strict. We need modes: strict / prefer / none.

Diego: Runtime should respect config: strict = filter candidates; prefer = scoring penalty against non-preferred; none = pure latency+capacity.

Mei: How do we handle capacity exhaustion in preferred region? Allow fallback with audit + sticky TTL so sessions don't bounce.

Tom: Suggest defaults: transient fallback window 30s, sustained 5m. Emit event routing.fallback with reason and TTL.

Lena: Add an admin-only override header X-RW-Force-Region (audited) for debugging. Also surface "routed outside preference" in account history with link to audit log.

Diego: Operational header helpful: X-Redwood-Route-Decision: region=eu-west-1;reason=consent;fallback=true;ttl=300

Aisha: Edge cases: dedicated pools need mapping from residency policy -> physical pools. RFC appendix should include config schema: mode, allowed_regions[], fallback_grace_seconds, allow_global_fallback boolean.

ops-bot: Canary flag enabled for jurisdictional-steering. Metrics will appear in ~10m.

Aisha: Next steps: Tom+Diego draft appendix, Lena drafts UI copy. We'll review tomorrow 30m.
